prompt.context: Our firm has just wrapped up a project with The Stance School, which offers K-12 education in Philadelphia, to help them with developing two major strategic initiatives. The first initiative, which is the priority, is an e-learning platform for their students to facilitate remote learning, in response to a global pandemic that resulted in students having to take classes from home for the last few months of the school year. The other initiative is a professional development tool to help the teachers with developing and effectively providing a remote curriculum to the students. The team that worked on the strategic planning determined that the cost would be $1M.
prompt.question: You are now tasked with determining how these initiatives will be funded within the next year and whether or not the school should move forward with this project.

clarifying_info.a: Currently it is 2020 H1 (First Half). The initiatives will be launched at the start of the 2020-2021 school year. The last income statement we have is from FY '18.

clarifying_info.q: Is the school public or private?
clarifying_info.a: The school is a private school in a major metropolitan city in the US, consisting of a lower and upper school educating levels K-12.
There are 1000 students in the school. Students are primarily middle to upper-middle class.

clarifying_info.q: What percentage of students are on scholarship?
clarifying_info.a: Approximately 10% of the students are on scholarship.

clarifying_info.q: Do we need to account for ongoing costs of the initiatives beyond the $1M?
clarifying_info.a: No need to consider ongoing costs. The $1M in savings per year should also cover the ongoing run-rate of the initiatives.

clarifying_info.q: Can the school use its endowment to fund the initiatives?
clarifying_info.a: The endowment is allocated for specific purposes and to ensure the school is funded long-term. It would not be an option for funding the initiatives.

framework: External Opportunities — Public Sector: lobby to raise federal/state appropriations, apply for grants
External Opportunities — Private Sector: solicit donations, seek endowment contributions (note: endowment not available per clarifying info)
Internal Opportunities — Raise Cash: increase tuition, grow alumni giving
Internal Opportunities — Cut Costs: reduce CAPEX, reduce OPEX (especially salaries)
Loans as a bridge financing option
A profit-tree (revenue minus costs) is also an appropriate framework; ensure both revenue and cost levers are explored

questions.prompt: What conclusions or insights can be drawn from examining The Stance School and its competitors' line items? (Exhibits 1 & 2)
questions.guidance: Strong candidates: (1) Convert expense line items to % of Tuition & Fees for each school and compare — Stance's Salaries/Wages/Benefits are ~35% of T&F vs. ~25% at Chestnut Hill, signaling over-spend; Scholarships are ~30% vs. ~40% at competitors (relatively lower but still large). (2) Note from Exhibit 2 that Stance already has the highest tuition and enrollment is declining — raising tuition further risks accelerating enrollment loss, so cost-cutting is the faster/safer path. (3) Note footnote 1: Stance is already receiving 100% of eligible grants, so grant revenue cannot be increased. (4) Identify salaries as the primary area to investigate and ask for breakdown by role/headcount.

math.setup: Express each expense as % of Tuition & Fees for Stance vs. competitors. Tuition & Fees ($ thousands): Stance $35,000; Rittenhouse $14,500; Chestnut Hill $29,000.
math.answer: Stance's salary line (~35% of T&F) is materially higher than competitors (~23-25%). This, combined with declining enrollment and already-maximized grants and near-ceiling tuition, points clearly to salary cost-cutting as the primary lever.

questions.prompt: The school has determined these 5 positions to reduce. Calculate annual cost savings if the school matches the benchmark ratio of students to position for each role. (Exhibit 4; 1,000 students total)
questions.guidance: Candidate should: (1) divide 1,000 students by the benchmark ratio to find target headcount; (2) subtract target from current to find headcount reduction; (3) multiply reduction by salary for each role; (4) sum to get total savings; (5) compare to $1M goal and identify the $90K shortfall.

math.setup: For each position: target headcount = 1,000 / benchmark_ratio. Reduction = current headcount - target headcount. Savings = reduction × salary.
math.answer: Total annual savings = $910,000. The school falls $90,000 short of the $1M goal.

brainstorming.prompt: What are the potential risks and associated costs that you anticipate when eliminating these roles?

categories.name: Financial Costs
ideas: Severance packages for eliminated roles
Pension obligations and related costs
Union negotiation costs and potential delays

categories.name: Non-Financial / Operational Costs
ideas: Time required to eliminate roles may delay savings realization within the budget year
Increased workload on remaining staff, risking burnout
Potential decline in service quality (e.g., custodial, IT support)

categories.name: Reputational & Enrollment Risks
ideas: Negative PR from high-profile layoffs at a school
Potential decline in enrollment as families react to staff reductions
Impact on school rankings or accreditation if student-support ratios decline

categories.name: Student Welfare
ideas: Negative mental health outcomes for students if guidance counselor ratios worsen
Reduced individual attention for students with higher counselor caseloads
Safety concerns if custodial/maintenance coverage drops below adequate levels

brainstorming.prompt: What are some ways that The Stance School could close the remaining $90,000 funding gap in order to reach the $1M goal?

categories.name: Revenue from Existing Assets
ideas: License the e-learning platform or teacher professional development tool to other schools
Offer fee-based remote tutoring or supplemental courses via the new platform
Rent school facilities during off-hours or summer months

categories.name: External Fundraising
ideas: Solicit donations from parents, students, and alumni
Target high-net-worth alumni for named gifts (e.g., named rooms, awards, endowed positions)
Launch a crowdfunding campaign tied to the remote-learning mission

categories.name: Government & Institutional
ideas: Lobby for additional state or federal appropriations or emergency education funds
Apply for technology-specific grants (separate from current grant eligibility cap)

categories.name: Cost Optimization
ideas: Identify additional operational efficiencies beyond the 5 roles
Renegotiate vendor contracts for maintenance, IT, or food services
Delay non-critical capital expenditures to free up cash

categories.name: Partnerships
ideas: Partner with a tech company for co-development of the platform in exchange for reduced cost
Seek corporate sponsorships in exchange for branding or access to curriculum data

recommendation: Move forward with the project: eliminate the 5 identified roles to generate $910K in annual savings, then source the remaining $90K through alternative means such as alumni donations, platform licensing, or additional operational savings

Alternative view: do not move forward until the school achieves full benchmark alignment — the $90K gap and layoff risks suggest the school should stabilize its cost structure before committing to new initiatives
risks: Negative PR and community backlash from staff layoffs at a K-12 school
Decline in enrollment if families perceive reduced student support, which would hurt revenue
Negative mental health or academic performance implications from higher staff-to-student ratios
Timing risk: contract reviews and severance processes may delay savings realization before the 2020-2021 school year launch
Missing out on critical technology and modernization if the project is not funded
next_steps: Conduct an in-depth analysis of the pros and cons of eliminating each of the 5 roles, including legal review of employment contracts
Start contract reviews and initiate the process of role elimination to finalize budget and reallocation before the next school year
Ensure enrollment is monitored closely so that any negative impact on revenue is detected early
Identify and execute on additional $90K of revenue or savings to close the funding gap
Evaluate whether the $1M estimate is fixed or can be phased to align with available savings
